messages:
maria-galvez: Quick thread — thinking through how much fidelity we keep in the control-plane -> runtime service-binding between hosted / dedicated / private. Short TL;DR: more fidelity gives safer rollbacks but tighter coupling. tradeoffs?

ajay-patel: Agree we should categorize fields. Can we split into 'safety-critical' vs 'advisory'? That'll guide what can be elided when downgrading.

sam-wu: Off the top: routing policy, credential surface, and KV cache hints. routing+creds = safety-critical; cache hints and batching are advisory.

elaine: Note: private mode already forces us to expose some network/topology hints to the control plane. Means a single opaque manifest won't work for all modes.

nick-h: Thinking in terms of graceful-deg tiers: full, compat, minimal. Full = everything. Compat = subset that preserves routing & security. Minimal = model id + region. Runtime needs to be able to signal which tier it accepted.

maria-galvez: Love the tier idea. Proposal: compat-tier fields = model_id, model_variant, max_tokens, routing_tag, fallback_chain, auth_claims. minimal = model_id, region_tag. Thoughts?

ajay-patel: +1, but auth_claims are sticky. We should NOT silently downgrade auth behavior; any reduction must be explicit and require operator approval (audit log).

sam-wu: Also: add a circuit header so runtime can tell control-plane "we're running compat tier" and why (e.g., capacity, tenant isolation). That helps debugging and alerts.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-proxy/canary v2 will include compat-tier header and metrics. (triggered by @maria-galvez)

elaine: Schema versioning: semver the manifest and include lightweight migration hooks. Control plane should keep translation adapters (compat -> full) instead of forcing the runtime to implement many permutations.

maria-galvez: Action items: 1) ajay + sam: produce compat-tier matrix (fields -> tier, downgrade safety rationale) 2) elaine: draft header spec + metrics mapping 3) nick: small doc snippet for user-visible fallback behavior and SLO expectations. I'll follow with an RFC update summarizing decisions.

sam-wu: One more: telemetry must include an "effective_tier" label and an "accepted_tier_reason" tag so we can correlate quality regressions to tier changes.

maria-galvez: Good call. Also we should add a short-run playbook for customer incidents when we detect unexpected compat downgrade (automated notification to oncall + owner).

nick-h: I'll sketch the doc snippet and include an example curl and a sample response header: `X-Runtime-Tier: compat; reason=capacity`

maria-galvez: OK wrapping up. No major objections, just the auth downgrade explicitness caveat. I'll post a concise RFC patch tomorrow with the matrix and header schema. Thanks y'all :tada:
